description:
'''Post-Britpop''' is an [[alternative rock]] subgenre and is the period in the late 1990s and early 2000s, following [[Britpop]], when the media were identifying a "new generation" or "second wave" of guitar bands influenced by acts like [[Oasis (band)|Oasis]] and [[Blur (band)|Blur]], but with less overt British concerns in their lyrics, more introspective songwriting, and greater influences from [[experimental music]] and American [[indie rock]].

Bands that had been established acts in the Britpop era, but gained greater prominence under post-Britpop, included [[Radiohead]] and [[the Verve]]. Meanwhile, newer acts such as [[Keane (band)|Keane]], [[Snow Patrol (band)|Snow Patrol]], [[Stereophonics]], and particularly [[Travis (band)|Travis]] and [[Coldplay]], achieved much wider international success than most of the Britpop groups that had preceded them, and were some of the most commercially successful acts of the late 1990s and early 2000s.
